hints: Constant acceleration means a horizontal a–t line, a straight v–t line, and a parabolic x–t curve. And the three must agree with each other.
worded:
1. Constant acceleration: the a–t graph is flat. All options have that, so look at the others.

2. v changes at a constant rate, so the v–t graph must be a straight line. (B) has a curved v–t graph: out.

3. x then changes at a steadily changing rate, so the x–t graph must be a parabola. (C) has a straight x–t line: out.

4. The graphs must also be consistent. In (A) velocity decreases, but the x–t curve gets steeper (velocity increasing): out.

5. (D): curved x–t getting steeper, straight rising v–t, positive constant a. All consistent. (D)
conventional:
For constant $a$: $v = u + at$ (straight line, slope $a$), $x = x_{0} + ut + \frac{1}{2}at^{2}$ (parabola, getting steeper when $a > 0$).

(A) slope of x–t increases but v–t falls: inconsistent. (B) v–t curved: a not constant. (C) x–t straight: v would be constant. (D) fits all three.
mistakes: Each graph alone may look right; check that the slope of one matches the next.
